subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support PowerShell `$` expansion payloads through explicit one-shot approval, or should OpenClaw document those payloads as unsupported in the exec contract?
rationale: Current code intentionally rejects these tokens for approval safety, while the issue and candidate PR ask maintainers to define a safer command-fidelity contract instead of silently closing the report.

options.title: Support via one-shot approval
options.body: Treat PowerShell expansion syntax as parseable but never durably trusted, and require native Windows/Gateway proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep the rejection behavior and update exec docs/tool guidance so users know to use script files or non-PowerShell workarounds for literal `$` payloads.

options.title: Defer pending proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer or contributor provides a real Windows/Gateway reproduction that distinguishes stripping from approval rejection.

recommendation.title: Support via one-shot approval
recommendation.body: Treat PowerShell expansion syntax as parseable but never durably trusted, and require native Windows/Gateway proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the Windows command authorization planner that jesse-merhi introduced and that PR #100322 modifies.
